sermon.title: Victorious in Afflictions, Persecutions, Tribulations
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 43 that God’s people are victorious in afflictions because God created, formed, redeemed and called them by name, and will be with them in the waters and the fire. He ties the waters to baptism, teaches that grace says no to ungodliness, and warns that living for Christ brings conflict. He ends with the hindrances to victory (not calling on God, impatience, forgotten offerings) and the invitation to “state your case” to God.

chunks.section_question: Does baptism have anything to do with salvation?
chunks.short_answer: He reads 1 Peter 3:20–21 and asks, “How can you tell me that baptism has nothing to do with salvation?” He says “water baptism is just as important as the sinner’s prayer,” that “people will defend their denominational doctrine above scriptural truth,” and that for him baptism was “my signature on the contract.”
chunks.text:

After I changed, they left me, and I had to learn to let them go, and it was painful, I didn’t want to lose friends, but I had to make a choice. I had to keep serving God. Folks, that is not Bible.

Did John the Baptist say, “Repent and be baptized for the remission of sin”? Were there two things that needed to be done? Yes. Jesus, when he came along, did he say, “Repent and be baptized for the remission of sin”? Two things had to be done, and he added one thing to it: “I believe the gospel.” Do we need to believe the gospel, trust in the gospel? Yes. You see, people will defend their denominational doctrine above scriptural truth.

chunks.section_question: What do the Red Sea and the Jordan teach about baptism and deliverance?
chunks.short_answer: He says the “waters” are the Red Sea and the “rivers” the Jordan, and “both baptisms delivered them from the affliction.” He says “passing through the Red Sea is a model of water baptism,” and “if you haven’t been baptized, I’d get baptized next Sunday.”
chunks.text:
And that first year I was going through a struggle, Mike hit it last week, well, you know, the king of Egypt could come after, and he didn’t want him serving God even after he’d let him go, he still was after his people. And that’s what Satan did. “You had nothing really happened, you weren’t really born again, you know, you’re just making a fool out of yourself.” How many went through that as a young Christian? Man, I don’t believe that. I don’t believe that only a few of us went through that. I know this book, and I know Satan, how he works. Now, the waters, of course, is talking about the Red Sea here, in Isaiah. Egypt was after them, they were afflicted in Egypt, okay, and “through the rivers” is talking about the river of Jordan, 40 years later they had to go through the river of Jordan. The Red Sea parted and they went through it, river of Jordan piled up in heaps in the north until Israel got across, and they were afflicted by the wilderness, and see, both baptisms delivered them from the affliction and the pain of what they had been going through.

Are you there? Hallelujah. And so I learned that. You know, these afflictions, they’re going to be, but God is going to deliver me out of every one of them, and I learned this in Isaiah, and then I found it all through the Scriptures. 1 Corinthians 10:1-2, “Our fathers were under the cloud, they passed through the Red Sea and were all baptized.” See, passing through the Red Sea is a model of water baptism. Noah’s judgment of water was an example of water baptism. Are you there? Water baptism is very important, and people that don’t get immediately baptized, they’re just missing it, and people that don’t believe that you need to get baptized

as part of your salvation plan, they are just wrong. So if you haven’t been baptized, I’d get baptized next Sunday. I’m serious. The thing that helped me, an old man in the Assembly God church led me to Christ, and he knew how to do it, took me right through the Scriptures. I knew what was happening, the power of God through the word that he was bringing to me and making me read delivered me. I got, say, I got born again that night, that load of sin went off of me that I didn’t even know I had. I didn’t know I had a burden of sin, it was gone. He said, “Son, you got to get baptized next Sunday.” “Well, okay, whatever.” What’s next? Whatever. The first thing was good, second thing, huh, whatever. I didn’t even, they didn’t even, they didn’t tell me what a baptism was. I tell people what baptism is so they understand. I got in that baptismal pool and the power of God came all over me, the presence of God just flooded me, but they didn’t teach, you know, other than tongue, some kind of, they didn’t teach you about the power and the presence of God.

But see, they came under the cloud, that’s the presence of God, and through the sea, the waters, the water baptism. The presence of God in water baptism is a powerful thing, church. And the Red Sea parting, the Bible says, was a model of water baptism. Hallelujah. And if nothing today, get your baptism doctrine right. You know, we pass on error to other people, we read error and we pass on error without really finding out and experiencing these powers in God, these principles. So, I’m delivered from the afflictions of sin. See,

Who were making their lives miserable and caused them to call upon God to deliver them?

chunks.section_question: Does believing in Jesus mean nothing bad will happen to you?
chunks.short_answer: He says people told him “nothing’s going to happen to you,” but “a couple of weeks after being saved I had more problems than I’d ever had before.” He cites 1 Thessalonians 3:3, “we are appointed to this,” and Psalm 34:19, “Many are the afflictions of the righteous,” and says Paul testified “God delivered me.”
chunks.text:

chunks.section_question: How do impatience with God and forgotten offerings hinder victory?
chunks.short_answer: He says the second hindrance is impatience: “you get impatient with God,” and “we take matters in our own hands.” The third is “No burnt offering”: he says Jesus is our burnt offering, “the way into the presence of God is thanksgiving,” and “If you are a silent saint, you’re not a growing saint.”
chunks.text:
I know you’re just perfect Christians. You don’t want to get impatient with your spouse, you get impatient with God. “God hasn’t changed him yet. God, how come you don’t straighten that spouse of mine out? I’ll do it for you, you [unclear], son of a [unclear].” When the Bible plainly says that bad words and good words don’t come out of the same fountain. That was good too. Hallelujah. There’s something wrong with the source when you do that, you understand? Hallelujah. So we get impatient, we get tired, and so we take matters in our own hands. If God wants to straighten my kids out, I’ll straighten them out.

Burn them, I’ll stab them. I’ve dealt with burnt kids, stabbed kids, whatever. Beaten with a razor strap or whatever. Number three, “No burnt offering.” Now I mean, you know that in Leviticus, as I just read Leviticus this week, there’s five offerings. The burnt offering is the covering for sin, the meal offering is the remembrance, it’s the remembrance offering. There, you remember that the burnt offering covers your sin. Who’s our burnt offering? Jesus Christ. We don’t do animal sacrifices because he already did it. The meal offering reminds me that Jesus Christ still forgives, still cleanses and delivers from sin even though I’m saved. And then you had the thank offering, the peace offering. That’s where you just thank God, “Thank you, Lord.” “I will enter his gates with thanksgiving in my heart.” You see, the way into the presence of God is thanksgiving. Hebrews, the last chapter, says, “By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise,” that thank offering, that peace offering, and then explains what it is: “the fruit of our lips giving thanks unto God.” If you are a silent saint, you’re not a growing saint.

You got to learn to lift up your lips. It’s a sacrifice, because you don’t want to do it. Man, it was humiliating when they said, you know, “Lift your hands and, and, you know, praise God.” Oh gosh, this guy died a thousand deaths. But I had to get to the place where I wanted God or I wanted myself. Then you have the sin offering and the trespass offering, the guilt offering. How many know your sins are forgiven? How many still get some guilt over sin? Yeah. See, God knew that, so he had a guilt offering. He comes and kills the guilt that you haven’t let go of from the sin offering.

You still feel guilty. Hallelujah, isn’t that good? Yeah. “And honor me by sacrifices,” which is the peace offering, the fruit of our lips. Now, this is hindrances to victory over afflictions. We won’t humble ourself and call on God. We get impatient with God when we’re doing our own thing. And we forget the burnt offering, Jesus can cleanse us and forgive us, and the praise offering. You burden God with your sins, you’re accepting sin in your life. That’s a hindrance to victory over afflictions. But God comes and he said, this is powerful, church, this is so powerful: “State your case, state your cause, that you may be acquitted,” set free. He says, you know, you got sin in you, you’re impatient with me, you won’t call upon me, so just come and state your case.

chunks.section_question: What does it mean to “state your case” to God?
chunks.short_answer: He reads “state your case, state your cause, that you may be acquitted,” and says “You got a complaint, don’t go to body members.” He tells of throwing down his guitar after a year without feeling God’s presence and listing what he was doing for God, and a still small voice said “It’s about time. You’re doing this all on your own strength,” after which peace and power came.
chunks.text:
All right, Moses stated his case. People, and all these people are, he stated his case, so what did God do? He came and gave himself the over 70 elders that caused him nothing but trouble for 40 years. And that’s what elders do in the church today, they are nothing but trouble if they are not a real elder, a Bible elder. They are nothing but trouble. They don’t have no spiritual growth to stand for righteousness and stand for truth at all, they just got a title. And that’s a good amen. Moses, when God wanted to destroy the people for sinning, he went and stated his case and said, “God, kill me instead of the people.”

And what did God do? He saved the people. State your case. You got a complaint, don’t go to body members. We learned last Sunday that when we start [unclear] complaining, we’re on our way back to Egypt. That was good last Sunday. That’s a sign you’re on your way back to the old life. Go to Jesus and state your case, complain to him. I remember as a young man, I’ve used this before, I’d been saved about three or four years, and I was, man, I was ministering at the prisons, at the juvenile halls, on the street corners, door-to-door, I was doing all these things. I had my guitar, my banjo, I put in tune, I was ministering, really soon, you know, hallelujah. But almost a year went by and I had not felt the presence of God, and this day I had to go minister, and I’m getting songs together, and I know there’s nothing in the songs, I know there’s nothing in my message, I know there’s nothing, because I know when there’s something.

And so I get mad at God. I threw my guitar down, broken, this was a thousand-dollar guitar back then. I mean, I was, I was stating my case like an idiot, but I was stating my case. And I went through the list, “Man, I’m saving souls, and I’m administering here, and I’m doing this, and I’m in the church, and I’m teaching Sunday school, and I’m leading the youth service, and I’m doing all this, and you’re not doing nothing.” That was my case. And that still small voice came to me and says, “It’s about time.” I said, “I quit, I quit.” He says, “It’s about time. You’re doing this all on your own strength, all in your own head knowledge. You left me back there.

You need to get back with me.” And just the tremendous peace and power, God come on me, began to weep. See why? Because I stated my case, I complained to him, and he come and set me free from my own initiated affliction. Are you there, Jeff? So don’t complain to people. If you’ve got a complaint, go to him. He can set you free. Powerful. We, we, we’re in sin, and he’s going to free us from those sins, we’re impatient, and he’s going to free us from that impatience. Hallelujah. “Remember me, who blots out your sin, remember me.

chunks.section_question: What does he say to remember about God when we face afflictions?
chunks.short_answer: He says “forget your pastor, forget your elders, forget the pope, forget the rabbis, remember who? Jesus Christ,” who can blot out your sin. He says God “created and formed you,” called you by name “so you don’t have to be afraid,” “he is not out to destroy you,” and “He will finish the good work he began in you.”
chunks.text:
Don’t forget me.” Church, forget your pastor, forget your elders, forget the pope, forget the rabbis, remember who? Jesus Christ. “I can blot out your sin, I can do it.” Hallelujah. You know, we go through 12-step programs, seven-step programs, this kind of program, that kind of program, and Jesus is up in heaven’s, and, “Folks, remember me. I’m the one that can acquit you, I’m the one that can set you free, and I will if you state your case honestly before me. I will deliver you.” Remember, he can heal sicknesses, the physical sicknesses, the mental sicknesses, the emotional affliction.

He can improve your poverty level. You can have peace in the middle of battles. Remember, God created and formed you, God is involved in this, he come to you personally and called you by name, so you don’t have to be afraid. He’s not out to destroy you. I don’t care how bad of a Christian you are, he is not out to destroy you. Do not be afraid. He will finish the good work he began in you. Be patient with yourself, be patient with others. He’s with us, and if he’s with us, we’ll get through anything. And for our charity, “I will deal with those that trouble you.” We may look like we’re losing the battle in America today, but there is coming a day of reckoning, and we want to be ready as righteous Christians in that day of reckoning. Amen. He will trouble those who trouble us, and we’ve got to state our case before God.

faqs.question: Why does he compare being redeemed to buying a car?
faqs.answer: He says “when you purchase a car you take care of it because it’s an investment.” He concludes “God’s going to want to take care of us, he’s purchased us, we’re his property.”

faqs.question: What did he see in China about baptism?
faqs.answer: He says “over there they waited six months to a year to baptize them. Folks, that is not Bible.” He says he asked a lot of questions about how quickly someone should be baptized.

faqs.question: Does he say John the Baptist and Jesus both said to repent and be baptized?
faqs.answer: He asks, “Did John the Baptist say, ‘Repent and be baptized for the remission of sin’?” and says “Jesus, when he came along,” said the same, and “he added one thing to it,” to believe the gospel.

faqs.question: How does he say he came to Christ?
faqs.answer: He says an old man in an Assembly God church led him to Christ, taking him “right through the Scriptures.” He says “that load of sin went off of me that I didn’t even know I had.”

faqs.question: What does he mean by “get your baptism doctrine right”?
faqs.answer: He says “we pass on error to other people, we read error and we pass on error without really finding out and experiencing these powers in God.” He says the presence of God in water baptism “is a powerful thing.”

faqs.question: What does he say about people who just join a church and say a prayer?
faqs.answer: He says “you just say a little mechanical sinner’s prayer, you got nothing,” and “That’s how we become a new creature” by being born again, whatever the denomination.

faqs.question: What does he say was wrong with what he was first taught about suffering?
faqs.answer: He says “they were teaching me wrong back there, the faith camp,” who said “nothing bad is going to happen.” He points to the lives of Jesus and the twelve apostles, who were afflicted.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Many are the afflictions of the righteous, But the LORD delivers him out of them all.

faqs.question: Does he say you must witness door-to-door to be in conflict with the world?
faqs.answer: No. He says “all you have to do is go through the day, live in your life for Christ, and you’re going to be at war with the enemy.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, But such as keep the law contend with them.

faqs.question: Was he timid about sharing Christ?
faqs.answer: He says “you may be too timid, like me, to share Christ with anybody. I broke that within a year.”

faqs.question: Whom does he say not to mess with?
faqs.answer: He says “if they’re pursuing Jesus and righteousness, don’t mess with them. They may not believe everything you believe, but those two things are the priority things.”

faqs.question: Does he say being righteous by the blood of Christ is enough?
faqs.answer: He says someone may say “I’m righteous by the blood of Christ,” and answers “that doesn’t help your wife you’re beating up.” He says real birth from God means “you do not continue in sin.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Little children, let no one deceive you. He who practices righteousness is righteous, just as He is righteous.

faqs.question: Where does he say self-control comes from?
faqs.answer: He says “Self-control comes from grace, as well as the Holy Spirit, as well as the Bible,” and that “self-control is just controlling yourself.”

faqs.question: What does he say about living for God in the present age?
faqs.answer: He says to live “so that they see the light in you and come and inquire of your God,” and that “he wants you to make a difference now.” He says that is “much better than him coming a second time.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For the grace of God that brings salvation has appeared to all men, teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly in the present age,

faqs.question: What does he say the guilt offering is for?
faqs.answer: He says God knew some still feel guilt after forgiveness, “so he had a guilt offering. He comes and kills the guilt that you haven’t let go of from the sin offering.”

faqs.question: What does he list as the hindrances to victory over afflictions?
faqs.answer: He says “We won’t humble ourself and call on God. We get impatient with God when we’re doing our own thing. And we forget the burnt offering.”
